title: Quarantine Telemetry and Escalation Lattice: Dashboard & Operator Spec
author: Ellen Chen
content:
Summary:
This document defines the telemetry dashboard and escalation lattice used during service quarantine events and staged reintegration. It standardizes signals, alert thresholds, operator flows, and dashboard panels so that platform operators and oncall engineers have a single, consistent surface for identifying quarantine candidates, executing soft-quarantine actions, and tracking SLO impact during reintegration.

Goals:
- Provide a single-pane dashboard for quarantine decisions and real-time impact analysis.
- Reduce noisy alerts by grouping telemetry into an escalation lattice (prioritized signals + tolerances).
- Define deterministic operator procedures for soft quarantine, partial eviction, and staged reintegration.
- Produce clear SLO/usage delta estimates to inform customer- and product-level comms.

Scope:
- Applies to multi-tenant LLM inference services and platform-side components that affect global throughput (routing, batching, cache).
- Focused on operational detection (Grafana + Prometheus), Alertmanager rules, and the operator checklist invoked by the oncall.
- Not a replacement for legal/regulatory containment steps for customer data compromise (see security-and-compliance).

Dashboard overview:
- Dashboard name: Quarantine Lattice — Live Incident View
- Primary consumers: Platform operators, oncall SREs, Runtime Owners
- Location: Grafana folder: /platform/operator/quarantine-lattice

Panels (high-level):
1) Candidate scoring heatmap (left) — aggregated per-service quarantine_score (0..100).
2) Signal rollup table (center) — per-service rows with metric columns: error_rate, tail_latency_p95, token_burn_delta, kv_cache_misses, eviction_rate, tenant_priority_score.
3) SLO impact simulator (right) — slider inputs for percent_traffic_moved showing projected SLO burn over next 1h/6h/24h.
4) Active quarantine contexts (bottom) — list of currently-quarantined services with start_time, operator, mode (soft/partial/hard), and recent actions.

Key metrics and PromQL suggestions:
- quarantine_score (computed service label): composite derived in recording rules. PromQL example (as recording rule expression):
  - name: quarantine_score
    expr: >-
      clamp_max(
        (increase(service_errors_total[5m]) / max(1, increase(service_requests_total[5m]))) * 50 +
        (histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(service_latency_bucket[5m])) / 0.5) * 20 +
        (increase(kv_cache_misses_total[10m]) / max(1, increase(kv_cache_hits_total[10m]) + 1)) * 15 +
        (token_burn_delta[5m] > 1000) * 15
      , 100)
- error_rate: increase(service_errors_total[5m]) / max(1, increase(service_requests_total[5m]))
- tail_latency_p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(service_latency_bucket[5m]))
- token_burn_delta: increase(service_token_consumption_total[5m]) - baseline_token_rate (baseline per-tenant config)
- kv_cache_misses: increase(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])

Escalation lattice (concept):
- Purpose: reduce cognitive load by ordering signals and mapping them to discrete operator actions. Each level has: signal set -> threshold -> suggested operator action(s) -> automatic safeties.

Levels (examples):
- Level 0 — Informational (score 0-29):
  - Signals: small error upticks (<0.5%), low cache miss changes.
  - Action: monitor, add annotation.
- Level 1 — Operator attention (score 30-54):
  - Signals: error_rate > 1% sustained 10m OR p95 increase > 2x baseline.
  - Action: open incident context, run quick health checks, consider soft-quarantine for noisy endpoints.
- Level 2 — Soft quarantine (score 55-74):
  - Signals: persistent elevated token_burn_delta > 2x baseline OR sustained cache eviction spike.
  - Action: enable soft-quarantine (traffic reduction via weight 0.7 -> 0.3), attach mitigation notes, start SLO impact sim.
- Level 3 — Partial eviction (score 75-89):
  - Signals: severe error_rate (>5%) OR p95 > 4x baseline OR token_burn_anomaly leading to capacity saturation.
  - Action: partial eviction of tenant (route 50% traffic away), suspend background batch jobs, enable emergency autoscale if available.
- Level 4 — Hard quarantine (score >=90):
  - Signals: sustained service-wide failures or data integrity concerns.
  - Action: hard quarantine (route 100% traffic away), notify product and customer-success, escalate to pager rotations.

Alerting rules and thresholds (examples for Alertmanager):
- alert: QuarantineCandidateHigh
  expr: quarantine_score > 55 and absent(up{job="runtime"}) == 0
  for: 5m
  labels: severity=page
  annotations: summary: "High quarantine score for {{ $labels.service }}"
- alert: QuarantineScoreSpiking
  expr: increase(quarantine_score[10m]) > 30
  for: 2m
  labels: severity=high

Routing & notification:
- Alerts at Level 1 -> Slack #platform-ops (no page), add ticket in incident-tracker with tag quarantine:investigate.
- Level 2 -> Platform SRE rotation notified (page), start 30m timer and follow operator checklist.
- Level 3 -> Platform SRE + Runtime Owner paged, primary engineer added.
- Level 4 -> All-hands page to #platform-incident and direct SMS pager, notify CSM for impacted customers.

Operator checklist: (invoked when score >= 55)
1) Confirm context: check active deploys, recent config changes, and ongoing experiments.
2) Validate telemetry: verify Prometheus query ranges and Grafana panel alignment.
3) Annotate incident: add start_time, operator, rationale to dashboard Active Quarantine Contexts panel.
4) Soft-quarantine step (if chosen):
   a) In the routing control UI execute: set-service-weight {{service}} 0.3 --reason "soft_quarantine" --expires 30m
   b) Run smoke test against canonical prompt set: ./scripts/smoke-test --service {{service}} --promptset quarantine-smoke-2026.json
   c) Observe SLO simulator for 10m; if SLO burn < 0.5% projected, keep reduced weight and schedule deeper investigation.
5) Partial eviction (if escalated):
   a) Scale down tenant routing: set-service-weight {{service}} 0.0 for public traffic, enable isolated test route.
   b) If capacity freed, validate throughput recovery and check cross-tenant degradation metrics.
6) Hard quarantine: route to fallback model variants; notify product & CSM; prepare rollback plan.
7) Document all actions and attach links to runbook in incident ticket.

Safety controls and automatic safeties:
- Auto-revert timers: every soft-quarantine has an expiry default 30m; operator can extend.
- Quarantine throttle: platform will only allow 3 concurrent soft-quarantines per region unless overridden by SRE lead.
- Auto-failback: if quarantine action causes >2x SLO burn for other tenants, platform automatically rebalances traffic back and paged.

Runbook CLI snippets (examples):
- Soft quarantine: rwlctl set-weight --service svc-foo --weight 0.3 --duration 30m --tag "soft_quarantine"
- Partial eviction: rwlctl set-weight --service svc-foo --weight 0.0 --duration 12h --tag "partial_eviction"
- Snapshot metrics: promtool query --expr 'increase(service_errors_total[5m])' --label service=svc-foo > /tmp/snapshot-svc-foo.log

Table: Suggested thresholds (service-level defaults)
| metric | level-1 | level-2 | level-3 | level-4 |
| error_rate | >1% sustained 10m | >2% sustained 10m | >5% sustained 5m | >10% sustained 1m |
| p95 latency (x baseline) | 1.5x | 2.0x | 4.0x | 8.0x |
| quarantine_score | 30 | 55 | 75 | 90 |
| token_burn_delta (tokens/5m) | 200 | 1000 | 5000 | 20000 |

Post-incident and retrospective hooks:
- Automated artifact capture: when a quarantine action is taken the system will attach a runbook bundle (logs, prom snapshot, and routing diffs) to the incident ticket.
- Retrospective template: use the Quarantine Retrospective template that captures timeline, root cause hypotheses, mitigation effectiveness (did soft quarantine reduce system pressure?), and follow-ups (technical debt, dashboard gaps).
- Mandatory blameless postmortem if hard quarantine lasted >1h or impacted >5% of total tokens served for >6h.

Run metrics to review after a quarantine event (first 24h):
- Time-to-detection (TTD): from first abnormal metric to quarantine action. Target <= 10m.
- Time-to-stabilize (TTS): from action to error_rate returning to baseline. Target <= 60m for soft quarantines.
- Regression rate on other tenants: % of tenants whose p95 increased >20% during action. Target < 5%.

Implementation roadmap (next 6 months):
1) Q2 2026 — implement quarantine_score recording rule and dashboard panels; add SLO simulator widget. Owner: Observability team.
2) Q3 2026 — integrate routing-control CLI with Grafana buttons (one-click soft quarantine). Owner: Eng Platform.
3) Q4 2026 — build simulation harness to run quarantine impact scenarios against historical traffic (capacity lab). Owner: Runtime + Platform.
4) Q1 2027 — policy engine: automatically suggest quarantine actions with confidence intervals and enforce concurrency limits. Owner: Platform Ops.

Ownership and contact points:

- Escalation policy owner: Platform SRE (owner: Luis Moreno, luis@redwood.ai)
- Routing-control service: runtime-router (team: Eng Serving Runtime)

Appendix A — Example Grafana panel JSON (abridged):
{"title": "Candidate heatmap", "type": "heatmap", "targets": [{"expr": "quarantine_score", "refId": "A"}]}

Appendix B — Quick verification checklist for automation engineers adding a new quarantine rule:
- Ensure recording rule has a clear description and test vectors.
- Add unit tests validating scoring function with synthetic telemetry.
- Add a dashboard-only feature flag so panels can be toggled during rollout.
- Confirm Alertmanager routing groups for severity=page and severity=high follow the lattice mapping.

Notes and rationale:
- The lattice approach reduces operator guesswork: by mapping composite scores to explicit actions we reduce escalations and speed decisions.
- Soft-quarantine prefers controlled traffic reduction instead of immediate hard routing changes to limit collateral damage.
